set.q: The sine function was discovered around 500 CE, and it is known for being periodic with a period of 2π. What is sin(545π)?
Find the sum as n goes from 1 to 8 of (1/2)^n.
Order the following 4 terms by increasing result: 1) lcm(2, 25); 2) lcm(5, 10); 3) gcd(7, 14); 4) gcd(4, 11)
This question is meant to be EASY. If Monish picks any two distinct letters from the word EASY, what is the chance that he gets the letters E and S?
What does log_2(3) times log_3(4) simplify to?
Order the following three strings by increasing number of distinct arrangements, given that no letter appears in a word more than once: 1) JUSTIN; 2) TOMB; 3) MATHS

Three lines are drawn in a plane labelled X, Y, and Z. Point P is reflected across X, Y, and Z, in that order, to a resulting point Q. What is the distance QQ' given that PP' is 1 and Q' is the reflection of P' across X, Y, and Z?
Evaluate 7!!, given that the double factorial of n is equal to n times n-2 times n-4 times ..., ending at either 2 or 1.
Justin is learning about a new unit in his calculus class: integrals! Which of the following is a possible antiderivative of the function f(a) = sin(2a)?
Which of the following tests would most likely be useful in determining the convergence status of Σ_(x=2)^∞ 1/(x ln x)?
If x^2 + 1/(x^2) = 3, then which of the following values is equal to x^4 + 1/(x^4)?
Identify all of the following 3 functions that match their range correctly: 1) sin(x) → [-1, 1]; 2) sec(x) → (-∞, -1] ∪ [1, ∞); 3) tan(x) → (-∞, ∞)

Identify all of the following three statements that are always true: 1) (If A, then B) and (If not C, then not B) implies (If A, then C); 2) (If A, then B) and (If not B, then not C) implies (If not B, then neither A nor C); 3) (If not B, then not A) or (If not B, then not C) implies (If B, then A or C)
How many petals does the polar equation r = 4cos(6θ) have?
The integral of the quantity a e^a da is equal to which of the following?
Consider the composition f(g(x)), where f(x)=3^x. Identify all of the following choices for g(x) that will result in f(g(x)) being a straight line: 1) log_3(x); 2) ln x; 3) x^(1/3)
Given that sin(2x) = 1/3, find sin^4(x) + cos^4(x)
By name or number, rank the following three numerical expressions by increasing value: 1) ln(7); 2) π/2; 3) e
How many solutions does ln(sin x)+ln(cos x)=-2 have on the interval from 0 to π/2?
Find the value of x such that e^(2x) - 4e^x + 4 = 0.
To the nearest tenth, if x is increasing at a rate of 1, then at what rate is the area between y=sin(x) and the x-axis increasing when x=π/4?
What is the value of √(5+√(5+√(5+√(5+⋯))))?

a.ac: ROTATION ABOUT A POINT AND HOMOTHETY

set.q: Ryan puts a particle on the origin. For 0 ≤ t ≤ 5, the particle is at position (t,t^2). Which of the following is the closest value to the distance that the particle has traveled?

A sequence is defined with the first term being 1 and every term after that is one more than twice the previous term-for example, the second term is 3, and the third term is 7. What is the value of the 10th term?
A polynomial P has integer coefficients. Identify all of the following three numbers that P(18) - P(6) must be divisible by: 1) 6; 2) 12; 3) 18
A Cunningham chain is a chain of primes p1, p2, …, p_n where p_(i+1) = 2p_i + 1, for i from 1 to n-1. What is the longest Cunningham chain subject to the condition that p1 is less than 20?
Identify all of the following functions that have an elementary antiderivative: 1) arctan(√x); 2) sin(√x); 3) arcsin(√x)
Which of the following best describes the characteristics of the polar curve defined by r^2 = 4cos(2θ)?

A permutation is called hilly if, when read from left to right, its numbers first strictly increase for a nonzero interval and then strictly decrease for a nonzero interval. How many permutations of the integers 1 through 8 are hilly?
For a triangle with area 8, what is the value of (abc)^2(sin A)(sin B)(sin C)?

Ryan is trying to solve Nesbitt's Inequality, which states that a/(b+c) + b/(a+c) + c/(a+b) is greater than or equal to 3/2, for positive reals a, b, c. Before applying Jensen's inequality, Ryan sets a + b + c equal to 1, and substitutes it in the denominators of his equation. This is only possible because scaling each of a, b, and c at the same time will have no effect on the inequality itself, because every term is of the same degree. What is the name for such inequalities?
What is the remainder when 1^6700 + 2^6700 + 3^6700 + ⋯ + 99^6700 is divided by 101?
How many critical points does the function g(x)=√(x(x-7)) have?
To the nearest integer, find the summation from n=2 to n=11 of n^(1/ln(n))
What is the value of tan(15°) + cot(15°), where 15 is in degrees?

Suzuko is standing on the top of a ladder that is lying against a wall. Currently, it is positioned so that the cosine of the angle the ladder makes to the horizontal is 4/5. Suddenly, the ladder slips and suzuko is now 3 units lower than he was before. If the cosine of the new angle the ladder makes with the horizontal is 24/25, what is the length of the ladder?
What is the name of the constant, which is roughly 1.202, that is equal to ζ(3)?
For the fibonacci numbers where F1 = 1 and F2 = 1, find the greatest common divisor of F24 and F36.

Arman and Abhinav are track stars. Each participates in 9 races, and they do not compete in the same race. In each race, they can win a gold medal, a silver medal, or no medal. Let G1 and S1 be the number of gold and silver medals Arman wins, and G2 and S2 be the corresponding numbers for Abhinav. If G1 is not equal to G2 and G1 + S1 = G2 + S2, how many possible tuples (G1, S1, G2, S2) are there?
In cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, angle ABC = 20 degrees, angle DAB = 40 degrees, and angle ABD = 10 degrees. What is the degree measure of angle ACB?
If the polynomial x^2 - 3x - 8 has roots r and s, find the value of r/(3r+8) + s/(3s+8).
In a 7-24-25 triangle with angles A, B, C, find 1/(sin(A/2)) + 1/(sin(B/2)) + 1/(sin(C/2)).
What is the value of sec(arctan(sin(arccos(3/5))))?

In cylindrical coordinates, Gabriel's Horn is defined by the equations r = z^(-n), 0 ≤ θ ≤ 2π, and z ≥ 1. For some values of n, Gabriel's Horn has a finite volume but an infinite surface area. What is the length of the interval of all n that satisfy this condition?

When solving an inequality, if a function is not uniformly concave or convex across its entire domain, Jensen's inequality may fail. In these cases, it may sometimes be possible to still prove that f(x) ≥ f(a) + f'(a)(x-a) for all positive integers x, where a is the mean of all inputs. What is the name for this technique?
The QM-AM-GM-HM inequality is a most directly a corollary of which of the following inequalities?
Order the following three sets by increasing cardinality: 1) Integers; 2) The set of all functions from the reals to the set {0, 1}; 3) The set of all infinite binary sequences
If B_n is the nth Bernoulli number, given that B1 = -1/2 and B2 = 1/6, then what is the value of B1 + B3 + B5?
Let r1, r2, …, r8 be the roots of x^8 + x^7 + x^6 + x^5 + x^4 + x^3 + x^2 + x + 1 = 0. Find the value of 1/(1-r1) + 1/(1-r2) + ⋯ + 1/(1-r8).
What series, given by the sum from n=1 to infinity of (csc^2 n)/(n^3), has not been proven to converge or diverge?
The discriminant of a quadratic can be extended to higher order polynomials. What is the discriminant of the polynomial (x-1)(x-2)^2(x-3)?
Let S be the upward-oriented lateral surface of the cone z = √(x^2 + y^2) for 0 ≤ z ≤ 3; if F(x, y, z) = (-y, x, 0), what is the surface integral over S of the normal component of the curl of F?
Which of the following is the sum of all integers n such that (n^2+3)/(n+1) is an integer?
What theorem states that a subset of R^n is sequentially compact if and only if it is closed and bounded?

Cauchy is studying the functional equation f(x) + f(y) = f(x+y) mapping real numbers to real numbers. Identify all of the following three conditions that guarantee that the only solutions to Cauchy's functional equation are linear: 1) f(x) = x for all x between zero and one.; 2) f(x) > 0 for all x greater than zero.; 3) The graph of f has no points inside the circle with equation (x-3)^2+(y-4)^2 = 1.
Consider the series defined as the sum from i=1 to n of the quantity 1/(sin(i)i^k). What is the behavior of this series in the limit as n tends to infinity?
There exists a unique positive real number x, such that x = 5/(√(x+1)-√x). Which of the following is closest to the value of x?

Careem selects random complex numbers with magnitude one z1, z2, z3, …. He keeps track of the partial sum S_n which is the sum of the first n complex numbers. Let R be the least value of C such that the expected value of the square of the magnitude of S_C is greater than 2025^2. What is the remainder when R is divided by 1000?
In the infinite series expansion for the expression 1/((1-x)^3), what is the sum of the coefficients of the first 6 terms?
Suppose a sequence satisfies the recurrence relationship that a0 = 2 - √3, and a_(n+1) = (2a_n)/(1-(a_n)^2). What is the value of a_2026?
Identify all of the following 3 positive integers for which the ring of integers of Q(√(-d)) is a unique factorization domain: 1) 43; 2) 67; 3) 103

Riyan applies the cosine function to 1, where 1 is in radians, compositely for a total of 1,000,000 times. In other words, he finds cos(cos(cos(.....cos(1))) where there are 1 millions cosine functions. Which of the following is the closest to this value?
If x+y+z = xyz = 5, then what is the value of (x+y)/(1-xy) times (y+z)/(1-yz) times (x+z)/(1-xz)?

Monish writes the number 2^(2^(2^(2^2))) on a blackboard. Every second, he erases the number currently on the board and replaces it with a randomly chosen positive integer divisor of that number. Which of the following is closest to the expected number of seconds until Monish writes (1) on the board for the first time?

Ordinal numbers are numbers too. What ordinal number is the smallest value for which Peano Arithmetic fails to prove transfinite induction, defined as the smallest non-zero fixed point satisfying x = ω^x, and equal to the limit ordinal of the sequence ω, ω^ω, ω^(ω^ω), …?

Harry likes analytic number theory – but only the genre where he gets to spam the Prime Number Theorem. Harry particularly enjoys pretending that each number n is independently prime with probability 1/(log(n)) and writing his problems from there. This is formally known as what model of prime density?

The fact that the integral of cosx from 0 to π/2 and the integral of sinx from 0 to π/2 are equal can be proved by what rule, which states that integrating a function over a closed interval yields the exact same total area when you replace the variable x with the sum of the lower and upper bounds minus x?
What is the units digit of 7^(2026)?
Which of the following is equal to the derivative of sin^2 x + cos^2 x at x = π/2?
Find the limit as x approaches 0 of (sin(x))/(x).
What is the remainder when 2^(99) is divided by 5?
Which of the following is the distance between the circle (x-2)^2 + (y-3)^2 = 4 and the line 3x+4y=2?
Robert is trying to plot the function given by f(x) = { x if x < 0; x + 1 if x ≥ 0 }. What type of discontinuity is formed by the function's behavior at x=0?
To pay for his debt of 120 at the John Sciencebowl Bank, Ryan has an infinite supply of 3s, 4s, and 12s. How many ways are there to pay for the debt if the order of the bills doesn't matter?
The function f(x) = x^2 - 3 and g(x) = √(x+3). What is the absolute difference between the values of f(g(49)) and g(f(49))?

The fact that 5 × 5 + 4 × 4 + 3 × 3 + 2 × 2 + 1 × 1 is greater than 5 × 1 + 4 × 2 + 3 × 3 + 2 × 4 + 1 × 5 is a specific example of what general inequality, which states that for two sequences, the sum of products is maximized when terms are ordered similarly and minimized when ordered oppositely?
How many digits are in the base-10 representation of 2^((2^((2^3))))?
What is the value of 1/(3^2) + 1/(6^2) + 1/(9^2) + ⋯ if the sequence continues to infinity for and each term is of the form 1/((3n)^2) for some positive integer n?
A sequence of numbers starts with a_0 = 41, a_1 = 67, and a_n = 5a_(n-1) - 6a_(n-2). As n approaches infinity, what is the ratio of the n+1st term to the nth term?
Evaluate the limit as n approaches infinity of the following two fractions: 1) (n!)/((n/e)^n); 2) (Γ(n))/((n/e)^n)
How many numbers from 1 to 2023 have a nonzero remainder when (n choose 20) is divided by 23?
Let F(n) denote the sum from k=1 to n of (n-k choose k). Find F(12).
What is the greatest integer k such that 2^k divides (4052 choose 2026)?
Shown in the image is a triangle ABC with altitudes and the orthocenter H drawn. Among the seven labelled points, how many sets of 4 points form a cyclic quadrilateral?

As shown in the image, Ryan randomly drops Monish's cyclic hexagon with a perimeter of 4 onto a unit square grid of hexagon-cutting lasers. What is the expected number of pieces that the boundary of Monish's hexagon is cut into?

Shown in the image is a fractal. Angles ABC, CBD, and DBA are all 120 degrees, and the length of BC divided by the length of AB is r. When r exceeds a critical value, the fractal is self-intersecting. Answer the following two questions about this fractal: 1) What is the critical value? 2) When the ratio is equal to the critical value, what is the dimension of the fractal?

Shown in the image is a geometric configuration. Ryan is trying to find the value of AD^2 + BE^2 + CF^2. He knows that A, B, and C are the vertices of a 13, 14, 15 triangle, as shown. Furthermore, point E is the point outside ABC such that ACE is an equilateral triangle, point F is the point outside ABC such that ABF is an equilateral triangle, and point D is the point outside ABC such that BCD is an equilateral triangle. The three circles drawn are the circumcircles of the equilateral triangles ACE, ABF, and BCD. The three circles drawn all intersect at one point, labeled G as shown. Answer the following three questions regarding this configuration: 1) What are the angle measures of AGC, BGC, and AGB, respectively? 2) This general construction of equilateral triangles followed by drawing their circumcircles will always result in an intersection of the three circles at one point for any acute triangle. What is the name of this point? 3) Find AD^2 + BE^2 + CF^2.

Answer the following two questions about this graph: 1) This graph can be used to show a lower bound on the Hadwiger-Nelson coloring problem. What is this lower bound? 2) What are the currently best-known lower and upper bounds, respectively, for this problem?

Shown in the image is a regular 10-sided polygon with side length 1, P1, P2, all the way to P10. Points P1', P2', etc. are constructed by reflecting P1 over P2, P2 over P3, etc. Answer the following two questions about this setup: 1) As the number of sides of the polygon increases while keeping side length fixed at one, the difference between the area of P1' P2' ... Pn' and P1 P2 ... Pn approaches a constant. Find this constant. 2) For finite n, is the real difference in area always smaller than the constant, always greater than the constant, the same, or does it depend on the value of n?

The last tiling problem was too easy. Given a one billion by one billion square, what is the natural log of the number of ways to tile it with 20 different types of square tiles, with side lengths ranging from 1001 to 1020? Give your answer to one significant figure. You may assume that the natural log of 20 is 3.

Shown in the image is a spiral generated by writing the positive integers in a square spiral and marking the prime numbers. Answer the following two questions about this spiral: 1) What is the name of this spiral? 2) The image shown is centered on 41. The long, unbroken diagonal chain of prime numbers corresponds to the values of what famous prime-generating polynomial?

Shown in the image is a triangle where AC = 13, AB = 14, and BC = 15. Ryan constructs D, E, and F such that D is the midpoint of BC, E is the midpoint of AC, and F is the midpoint of AB. He then draws the circumcircles of CED, AFE, and BDF, and finds that they all intersect at a point G. Answer the following three questions about this configuration: 1) Respectively, find the values of AG, BG, and CG. 2) The point G is a special point for triangle ABC. What is the common name given to this point? 3) Find the sum of the 6 arc lengths shaded in red.

Shown in the image is a polygon with n sides. The first vertex is the origin, (0, 0). The second vertex is (1, 1/2), the third (1/2, 1/3), the fourth (1/3, 1/4), the 5th (1/4, 1/5), the 6th (1/5, 1/6), and so on, with the nth vertex being (1/(n − 1), 1/n) for n greater than or equal to 2. What is the limit of the area of this polygon as n goes to infinity?

Shown in the image is the definition of three functions. Ryan wants to integrate the Riemann Zeta function from s = 1 to 2, but knows that it is undefined at s = 1. To resolve this, he truncates the sum at an upper limit k, integrates the truncated function, and then takes the limit as k approaches infinity. Which of the following best describes the behavior of f(k) as k approaches infinity?
